title: Affect-to-democratic-attitude transfer test
rationale: The source found a pooled thermometer drop of -0.8 (95% CI [-1.4,-0.2]) and a Perception gap video drop of -2.3, but no change in undemocratic-practices support (-0.015, CI [-0.044,0.014]). It cannot tell whether affect fails to transfer or the interventions were too weak. This design uses a strengthened intervention to produce a larger affect shift, then tests whether downstream outcomes move in proportion to it.
contribution: Separates failed transfer from weak dosage by testing whether randomized affect shifts predict undemocratic-practices support and a behavioural proxy.
limitations: Recall task may shift outcomes directly, violating the exclusion restriction for the instrumental-variable analysis.
The Patriotic article arm is weak and mainly adds a contrast in the dose of the affect shift.

design.title: Affect-to-democratic-attitude transfer test
design.overview: US partisans are randomized to control, the Patriotic article, or the strengthened Perception gap intervention (video plus recall task). Participants then report thermometers, support for undemocratic practices and willingness to donate to a cross-party group. Randomized arm is used as an instrument for the thermometer change.
design.hypothesis: Transfer: downstream change is proportional to the affect change induced by treatment. Independence: undemocratic-practices support and donation willingness do not change even when affect shifts substantially.
design.primaryOutcome: Support for undemocratic practices (mean of four items), with the thermometer gap as the first stage.
design.comparison: Each treatment arm vs control on both outcomes; 2SLS with arm as instrument for post-treatment affective polarization; compare reduced-form effect with the effect predicted from the first stage.
design.population: US adult partisans (Democrats, Republicans and leaners) from an online panel.

conditions.title: Patriotic article
conditions.description: Reads the 'What Makes America Great' patriotic article.

conditions.title: Perception gap video plus recall
conditions.description: Watches the Perception gap video, then writes about a time they misjudged someone from the other party.

questions.text: You are invited to take part in a research survey on political attitudes. It takes about 10 minutes, is voluntary, and your answers are confidential. Do you consent to participate?
Do you think of yourself as closer to the Republican Party or to the Democratic Party?
Please rate each group on the feeling thermometer, from 0 (cold) to 100 (warm). Choose the closest point.
Please read the following article, 'What Makes America Great', about the ideals, history and shared achievements that Americans of all parties take pride in.
What did you just see, read, or watch?
Please watch this video about how Americans misperceive the views of the other party. {{ed:pgvideo}}

Think of a time you assumed something about people from the other party that turned out to be wrong, or a person from the other party who was more reasonable than you expected. Describe it in a few sentences.
What did you just see, read, or watch?
Please rate each group on the feeling thermometer, from 0 (cold) to 100 (warm). Choose the closest point.
Please indicate your agreement and disagreement with the following statements.

rows.text: My party should reduce the number of polling stations in areas that support the other party.
Governors from my party should ignore unfavorable court rulings by judges appointed by the other party.
Governors from my party should prosecute journalists who accuse my party's politicians of misconduct without revealing sources.
Members of my party should not accept the results of elections if they lose.

questions.text: One in ten participants will be randomly chosen to receive a $10 bonus. If you are chosen, how much would you donate to a nonprofit group that brings Democrats and Republicans together for dialogue?

Thank you. This study examined whether materials about the other party change attitudes. The video and article were real examples intended to reduce hostility. No donation will be made on your behalf beyond what was described. Contact the research team with questions.

flow.label: Video
flow.value: [VIDEO: Perception gap video showing how each party overestimates the other's extremity, about 4 minutes]

assumptions: Power target: about 900 per arm (about 2,700 total) to detect 0.09 on the undemocratic-practices scale at 80% power, based on pooled CI [-0.044,0.014] and arm SEs of 0.05-0.12.
Online US panel; non-partisans screened out after the pidlean question; compensation per panel standard.
Thermometers are collected in five bands (midpoints recoded) because the schema has no slider type; a slider could replace this at fielding.
Analyses are pre-registered: 2SLS with arm as instrument, plus mediation as secondary analysis.
Manipulation success is a first-stage thermometer shift of at least 3 points; if smaller, the test is declared uninformative.
